doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Losses in the 1990s
summary: His uncle, daughter and mother died, and he nearly stopped playing.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So you’re talking about the late ’80s now, this period that you were going through.

Yeah, going on to the late ’80s, because in the ’90s I really crossed, because that’s the year my favorite uncle passed and then my daughter passed – my other daughter – and then my mother passed. So I was almost ready to stop playing. Because I’d go play and I couldn’t even remember the tune we were playing. Like they say, “Vonski, are you going to come in?” I say, “What are you playing?” They say, “We’re
playing I Hear a Rhapsody.” I say, okay. Come in and play, and my mind wasn’t nowhere near on it. They say, “Man, you’re really playing.” I say, whew. I say okay.
